THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Wausau city leaders moved toward an independent audit of city government, while Marathon County wrestled with a troubled rural broadband project and a packed slate of budget presentations heading into 2027.

  • Wausau's Committee of the Whole unanimously directed the executive committee to develop a scope and procurement process for an independent systemic audit of city government, with the full proposal returning to council before any contract is signed.
  • Marathon County's Infrastructure Committee ordered Bug Tussle to submit a detailed scope-change document — covering mileage, tower modifications, and a subscriber take-rate plan — before the broadband project can advance to the full County Board.
  • The Wausau Water Works Commission heard that the city's water utility is roughly 13% rate-deficient, a gap that could grow to 20% by 2027; staff will bring rate-case options to the October 6th meeting for a possible decision.
  • A proposed Riverlife South development agreement with Wangard failed on a 2-1 vote at Wausau's Economic Development Committee, while staff were directed to pursue DNR meetings and a deed restriction limiting the contaminated 1300 Cleveland Avenue site to non-industrial use.
  • Marathon County's Extension, Education, and Economic Development Committee directed staff to research legal authority before committing any county funds to Advance Wisconsin's $25,000 annual request for the LifeWorks justice-involved workforce program.
  • Marathon County's Health and Human Services Committee confirmed existing contract funding for North Central CAP ($33,757) and United Way 211 services ($40,000) in the draft 2027 budget, with the ADRC's $41,000 levy increase already built in.

Coming up: Tuesday, September 8 is the busiest day of the week, with Wausau's Common Council meeting at 6:30 p.m. — expected to receive the audit proposal framework — and the city's Finance Committee convening at 5:15 p.m.; Wednesday, September 9, Marathon County's Extension, Education, and Economic Development Committee meets at 5:00 p.m. alongside a previously scheduled joint session with HR, Finance, and Property committees at 3:00 p.m. to continue closed-session discussions.
